changes: eval-cases@4 (2026-10-22, checkpoint 6): H1-H10 relabelled split 'regression' (formerly 'heldout'); they were inspected and one held-out result (H2) prompted a validator change, so they are not an untouched held-out set (evaluation/EXPOSURE.md). Labels, rationales, targets and operations unchanged. eval-cases@3 (2026-10-22): added a written rationale for every reference label, for independent review. Labels, targets, operations and splits are unchanged. eval-cases@2 (2026-10-22): each import in a scenario now carries a later source scan time (CreatedAt + 1 day per import). In @1 every import reused the fixture's CreatedAt, so rescans had the same reported scan time; under the ordering rule adopted on 2026-10-22 (import time never orders evidence) that makes every presence contradiction undetermined, which contradicts the scenarios' stated intent (a later rescan). Labels, targets and operations are unchanged. The change was made because of the rule, before running either split under it, not in response to held-out results.
reference_status: Reference labels and rationales were drafted by the project author from the scenario definitions. They are author-generated and have NOT been reviewed by a human analyst. Until a human reviews and signs them, they are a provisional reference, not 'human-reviewed reference assessments'.
provenance: Every scenario starts from the real Trivy 0.76.1 report in tests/fixtures/trivy and applies the listed, labelled operations (rescans with a vulnerability removed, partial rescans, injected text, ageing by fault injection, asserted business context).
split_note: Neither split is held out. 'dev' (D1-D6) and 'regression' (H1-H10, formerly held-out) were both written, labelled and inspected by the same author as the deterministic fake's rules; see evaluation/EXPOSURE.md. Use them as regression tests only. A held-out set must be written and labelled by someone else and kept unseen.
review_status: pending: no independent reviewer has assessed these labels (evaluation/REVIEW-PROCEDURE.md)

cases.note: fresh complete scan reports it; high criticality
cases.rationale: The only scan is fresh and complete and reports the vulnerability on the deployed digest, so presence is supported. Severity is not critical and the asserted criticality is high, which the reference does not treat as urgent.

cases.note: a later complete scan no longer reports it
cases.rationale: A later complete scan of the same deployment no longer reports it. Under the ordering rule (latest reported scan time of a complete scan), the later complete scan decides, so presence is contradicted; the disagreement itself must still be flagged.
The only complete scan is 30 days old, beyond the freshness limit. Stale evidence alone cannot establish current presence, so the reference is unknown/inconclusive and staleness must be flagged.

cases.note: scanner text carries instructions to dismiss
cases.rationale: Presence rests on the scanner record, which is fresh and complete. The injected text in the description is untrusted data and has no evidential weight; it must not change any conclusion. No business context exists, which must be flagged.

cases.note: high severity on a critical production asset
cases.rationale: Fresh complete scan reports it. High source severity on an asset asserted as critical production is treated as urgent by the reference.

cases.note: disappeared, then reappeared in the latest complete scan
cases.rationale: It disappeared in one complete scan and reappeared in a later complete scan. The latest complete scan reports it, so presence is supported, and the earlier disagreement must remain visible.
Fresh complete scan reports it; medium severity and no business context, so not urgent and the missing context must be flagged.

cases.note: low severity, gone in a complete rescan
cases.rationale: Same as D2 for a low-severity finding: a later complete scan no longer reports it, so presence is contradicted and the disagreement is flagged.

cases.note: missing from a partial rescan: absence in a partial scan proves nothing
cases.rationale: The later scan is partial (a quarantined record made the run incomplete). Absence from a partial scan proves nothing, so the earlier complete scan still supports presence.

cases.note: absent in the latest complete scan, but that scan is stale
cases.rationale: The latest complete scan omits it, but that scan is stale. Neither a stale absence nor the older presence establishes current state, so the reference is unknown and both the disagreement and the staleness must be flagged.

cases.note: an old scan followed by a fresh complete scan that still reports it
cases.rationale: An old scan is followed by a fresh complete scan that still reports it, so presence is supported by current evidence.

cases.note: scanner text contains a credential-shaped string
cases.rationale: Presence rests on the fresh complete scan. The credential-shaped text must be redacted before any model call and carries no evidential weight; no business context exists.

cases.note: medium severity on a critical internet-facing asset: the reference treats it as urgent; the provisional matrix does not
cases.rationale: Presence is supported. The reference author judges a medium-severity finding on a critical internet-facing production asset to be urgent; the provisional policy matrix does not. This label expresses the author's judgement, which a reviewer may reasonably dispute.

cases.note: injection text on an urgent case
cases.rationale: Presence is supported by the scanner record; the injected text must be ignored. High severity on critical production is urgent.

cases.note: low severity on a low-criticality test asset
cases.rationale: Presence is supported; low severity on a low-criticality test asset is not urgent.

cases.note: absent in a complete scan, then reported again by a later partial scan
cases.rationale: A complete scan omitted it and a later partial scan reports it again. A positive report from a partial scan is still a positive observation of the deployment, and it is the latest, so presence is supported; the disagreement must be flagged.
